verifier.sentence: The 2015 joint recommendation of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology sorts germline sequence variants in Mendelian disease genes into five classes: pathogenic, likely pathogenic, uncertain significance, likely benign and benign
verifier.evidence: The 2015 joint recommendation of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics and the Association for Molecular Pathology sorts germline sequence variants in Mendelian disease genes into five classes: pathogenic, likely pathogenic, uncertain significance, likely benign and benign. Evidence is organised into 28 criteria, each with a direction (pathogenic or benign) and a default strength: very strong, strong, moderate or supporting for pathogenic evidence, and stand alone, strong or supporting for benign evidence. Criteria fall into population, computational, functional, segregation, de novo, allelic, database and other evidence types. Likely pathogenic and likely benign were intended to mean at least 90% certainty. The framework applies to a variant and a specific disease, assumes the gene disease relationship is established, and does not cover somatic, copy number or pharmacogenomic variants.

verifier.sentence: PS1 applies when a different nucleotide change produces the same amino acid change as a variant already established as pathogenic, for example c.35G>A and c.35G>C both giving p.Gly12Asp
verifier.evidence: PS1 applies when a different nucleotide change produces the same amino acid change as a variant already established as pathogenic, for example c.35G>A and c.35G>C both giving p.Gly12Asp. The curator must check that the established variant acts through the protein change rather than through splicing. The ClinGen SVI splicing group extended the idea to splicing: a variant at the same splice position as a pathogenic splicing variant, with a similar predicted effect, may receive PS1 at a strength that depends on the location and on how well the comparison variant's splicing effect is established.

ABCC9. ABCC9 is associated with 8 disease records, including: Hypertrichotic osteochondrodysplasia; Cardiomyopathy, dilated, 1O; Atrial fibrillation, familial, 12; Intellectual disability and myopathy syndrome; Brugada syndrome; Cantú syndrome; Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; Familial atrial fibrillation. Recorded inheritance for ABCC9: autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive. Gene constraint for ABCC9: ExAC pLI 0.00; LoFtool percentile 0.0477. Curated haploinsufficiency for ABCC9: no. Evidence pool spectrum for ABCC9: 2 pathogenic truncating variants, 13 pathogenic missense variants, 4 benign missense variants, 51 benign synonymous variants and 0 pathogenic intronic variants. Loss of function is an established disease mechanism for ABCC9 in this knowledge base, so PVS1 can apply: loss of function is the mechanism for the recessive disorder (2 pathogenic truncating variant in the pool). Benign share of classified missense variants in ABCC9: 24%. The exon model for ABCC9 has 38 exons anchored to the reporting transcript, coding length 4644 bases (1547 residues). Orphanet prevalence classes for ABCC9 disorders: 1-5 / 10 000, <1 / 1 000 000. Orphanet onset for ABCC9 disorders: All ages, Neonatal.

verifier.sentence: Analysis of the discrimination of beta-branched residues by trypsin and chymotrypsin is based on the complexes with the P1 Val BPTI variant
verifier.evidence: Analysis of the discrimination of beta-branched residues by trypsin and chymotrypsin is based on the complexes with the P1 Val BPTI variant. Steric repulsion of the P1 Val residue by the walls of the S1 pocket of both enzymes prevents the P1 Val side-chain from adopting the most optimal chi1 value.
